title: Online Banking Technology: What Banks and Credit Unions Should Know
summary: Learn how online banking technology works, what capabilities banks and credit unions should evaluate, and how Alkami helps financial institutions.
body_markdown:
Jump to Alkami’s differentiators >>


Online banking technology is the software and infrastructure that lets account holders manage money, make[payments](https://www.alkami.com/digital-banking-solutions/business-banking/payments/) , receive support, and access financial services through web and mobile channels. For a financial institution, the technology also connects digital experiences to core systems, payment providers, data, security controls, and partner services.


The best online banking platform gives[banks](https://www.alkami.com/banks/) and credit unions a dependable digital foundation for acquisition, activation, service, engagement, and relationship growth.


The online banking channel shapes how account holders experience the financial institution. According to[Alkami research](https://www.alkami.com/resources/research/2026-generational-trends-in-digital-banking-report/) 1 in partnership with the[Center for Generational Kinetics](http://genhq.com/) , 76% of digital and online banking Americans say that the online banking experience reflects how much a financial institution cares about the account holder. The platform must make everyday banking easy while giving the financial institution enough flexibility to personalize experiences, integrate new capabilities, protect account holders, and measure business outcomes.


## What is online banking technology?


Online banking technology combines the digital channels, platform services, integrations, data, and security capabilities that allow account holders to access and use financial services remotely. It typically connects a financial institution’s core banking environment with web and mobile interfaces, payments, authentication, alerts,[customer service](https://www.alkami.com/digital-banking-solutions/retail-banking/customer-service/) , analytics, and third-party providers.


Modern online banking platforms are often described as the layer between the core and the experiences used by account holders and employees. That layer helps financial institutions create and manage digital journeys much more easily.


Online banking platforms can support activities such as:


- Viewing balances and transaction history
- Transferring money between accounts
- Paying bills and sending payments
- Depositing checks through a mobile device
- Managing cards and digital wallets
- Receiving alerts and completing security actions
- Applying for products or opening accounts
- Accessing financial insights and personalized guidance
- Managing business payments, approvals, and cash flow


The specific feature set varies by provider and financial institution.


### Why does online banking technology matter to financial institutions?


Online banking technology matters because it is one of the most visible and frequently used parts of the modern account holder relationship. It can influence how quickly a new account holder becomes digitally engaged, how frequently existing account holders interact with the financial institution, and whether they view it as their primary financial partner.


A modern platform can help financial institutions:


- Make routine tasks easier for consumers and business users
- Give employees better tools to support digital relationships
- Connect behavioral and transactional data to relevant actions
- Reduce manual work and unnecessary service handoffs
- Introduce new capabilities through integrated third-party solutions
- Strengthen security without causing friction for legitimate account holders
- Measure how digital engagement contributes to growth


A digital banking experience can help a financial institution guide account holders toward the next useful action, whether that means activating a card, setting up direct deposit, reviewing a financial insight, responding to a fraud alert, or exploring a relevant product.


### What capabilities should a modern online banking platform include?


A modern online banking platform should combine a strong user experience with extensibility, data connectivity, security, and operational control. Financial institutions should evaluate how the platform supports activation, ongoing engagement, service, retention, and relationship growth, as well as how it connects with account opening and other solutions across the broader account holder lifecycle.


1. **A consistent experience across web and mobile**


Account holders move between devices and expect familiar functionality wherever they sign in. A platform should provide a coherent experience across web and mobile while allowing the financial institution to reflect its own brand, priorities, and service model. When assessing online banking platform providers, the evaluation should go beyond visual design. Consider how easily account holders can complete high-value tasks, find support, understand their financial position, and move from an insight to an action.


1. **Core connectivity and open integrations**


Online banking technology needs reliable connections to the core and to the broader financial technology ecosystem. Open APIs, integration frameworks, and partner connectivity can help financial institutions add capabilities.


1. **Data that leads to useful action**


Data becomes more valuable when it helps someone decide what to do next. Online banking technology should help financial institutions use behavioral and transactional signals to deliver relevant content, guided journeys, alerts, and service actions. For example, a signal may indicate that an account holder could benefit from an “add your card to digital wallet” prompt, a deposit retention journey, a financial insight, or a fraud remediation step. The value comes from connecting the signal to the right experience and measuring what happens afterward.


1. **Security and fraud support within the trusted channel**


Security should be part of the online banking experience that operates behind the scenes. The platform should support layered authentication, appropriate controls, contextual alerts, and clear remediation paths. When account holders receive a security message in the channel they already trust, they may have a clearer path to taking action. Depending on the situation, that action could include locking a card, reporting a transaction, confirming activity, or completing an authentication step.


Financial institutions should evaluate how a provider balances protection with convenience. Controls that create unnecessary friction can make ordinary banking harder. Controls that lack context may also increase contact center demand.


1. **Support for retail and business banking**


Retail and business end users have different needs. A retail experience may emphasize everyday[money movement](https://www.alkami.com/digital-banking-solutions/retail-banking/money-movement/) , card controls, financial insights, and self-service. Business and commercial banking users may need payment approvals, ACH, wires, cash flow tools, reporting, user entitlements, and more complex workflows. A shared platform foundation can help financial institutions simplify vendor management while preserving the functionality each audience requires. This is especially important for financial institutions that want to grow relationships across retail, small business, and commercial segments.


1. **Configuration, measurement, and operational control**


A platform should help lean teams make meaningful changes without turning every improvement into a custom development project. Look for platform configurations, reusable components, audience controls, guided workflows, reporting, and governance. Measurement should connect digital activity to an outcome.

1


What is online banking technology?


Online banking technology is the combination of digital channels, platform services, integrations, data, and security capabilities that allows account holders to access and use financial services through web and mobile experiences.


2


What should banks and credit unions look for in an online banking platform?


Banks and credit unions should evaluate user experience, core connectivity, APIs, data activation, security, retail and business capabilities, configurability, implementation requirements, and measurable business outcomes.


3

APIs allow a digital banking platform to connect with core systems, fintech providers, payment services, internal applications, and other parts of the technology ecosystem. They can help financial institutions add capabilities while preserving a more consistent digital experience.
